purpose: Explain the Refactor Report tab, project-folder scanning, pasted or loaded state-vector JSON, daily refactor report output, AI bundle generation, and re-extraction controls.
display_lines: Refactor Report builds a structured state vector that describes project structure, complexity, governance, churn, dependency shape, and refactor pressure.
Use Mode A when you want the tab to scan a project folder and generate the state vector from Python source files.
Use Mode B when you already have state-vector JSON or pasted chat output that should be loaded, edited, or compiled.
Step 2 controls the report name and output folder; the tab creates its daily_refactor output tree under that location.
Step 2b optionally writes the final AI bundle to an exact file path instead of the default bundle folder.
Compile State Vector runs the normal pipeline, Force Re-extract bypasses cached extraction, and Save Bundle Now writes a bundle from the last compiled state.
The generated bundle is the compact AI handoff artifact; it is evidence and context, not a source-code edit.

errors.plain_explanation: Select a real project folder when you want the report to scan source files directly.
errors.if_not_corrected: The compiler cannot build a state vector from project files and may ask for pasted or loaded JSON instead.
errors.easy_example: Use Select Project Folder on the repository root before compiling a fresh project scan.

errors.plain_explanation: Paste or load a valid state-vector JSON document when you are not scanning a project folder.
errors.if_not_corrected: The compiler has no canonical state vector to merge, validate, or save.
errors.easy_example: Use Load Existing JSON to open a previous current_state, state_history, or bundle JSON.

errors.plain_explanation: Set a clear report name and output folder before compiling so generated files have a stable location.
errors.if_not_corrected: Outputs may be missing, written to an unexpected folder, or hard to match to the reviewed project.
errors.easy_example: Name the report auth_module and choose a workbench or project-analysis output folder.

errors.plain_explanation: Use the optional bundle path only when you need the final AI handoff JSON written to a specific file.
errors.if_not_corrected: The bundle still uses the default location, which may be fine but may not match a planned handoff path.
errors.easy_example: Set Bundle Path when another workflow expects refactor_report_bundle.json in a fixed folder.

errors.plain_explanation: Use Force Re-extract when cached analysis may be stale after file moves, generated source changes, or a failed prior run.
errors.if_not_corrected: The report may reuse older extraction data and understate current refactor pressure.
errors.easy_example: Run Force Re-extract after a large refactor or after changing many Python modules.

errors.plain_explanation: Use Save Bundle Now only after a successful compile when the bundle file is missing or needs to be regenerated.
errors.if_not_corrected: You may hand off stale or incomplete evidence to an AI reviewer.
errors.easy_example: Compile first, then Save Bundle Now if the report exists but the bundle file was not created.
